claims.sentence: <jats:sec> <jats:title>Background</jats:title> <jats:p> Metformin has been proposed to have neuroprotective benefits, but its effects on AD-related brain changes remain unclear and may be influenced by apolipoprotein E ε4 ( <jats:italic toggle="yes">APOE4</jats:italic> ) genotype, a major genetic risk factor for AD. </jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Objective</jats:title> <jats:p> To examine the association between metformin use and in vivo AD pathologies and to evaluate whether <jats:italic toggle="yes">APOE4</jats:italic> status moderates these associations in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). </jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Methods</jats:title> <jats:p> This cross-sectional study used baseline data from 76 non-demented older adults with T2DM (aged 55-90 years), who were enrolled in the Korean Brain Aging Study for Early Diagnosis and Prediction of Alzheimer's Disease (KBASE).
